items.title: GM's next-generation EV platform detailed: LMR batteries only, fewer parts, mainstream focus
items.summary: GM unveiled a fourth‑gen EV platform with cheaper lithium‑manganese batteries, promising lower costs, longer range and broader application, boosting its global outlook.

evidence.quote: Speaking at the GM Forward event in New York, GM president Mark Reuss said the new platform would underpin vehicles in the automaker's highest-volume segments, bringing "lower costs, long range, and improved performance" to mainstream EV buyers.
- General Motors is developing lithium manganese-rich batteries for multiple affordable EVs, including a mainstream battery-powered SUV expected in about three years.

The LMR battery is designed to offer 33 percent more energy density than lithium iron phosphate, which is expected to translate into longer range from a smaller and lighter battery pack that costs about the same as one that uses LFP chemistry.

proposal.statement: GM unveiled a fourth‑gen EV platform using lithium‑manganese batteries that promises lower costs, longer range and broader application for mainstream EV buyers.
